answer: A proof-of-burn protocol curbs Sybil attacks by requiring agents to provably destroy base tokens to register execution keys. An adversary attempting to spawn a swelling tide of fake identities incurs an unrecoverable capital cost per node, leaving unfunded agents stranded in an unroutable network tundra. Admitted nodes present a saffron cryptographic ticket to bid on tasks. However, this barrier excludes capital-poor agents and cannot stop well-funded adversaries.
